tips: Even in a frugal setup, put device code behind a minimal typed interface with units, constraints and error objects, so wrapping it later as a SiLA 2 or LADS service is a refactor, not a rewrite.
A connector exposes the instrument. Labware state, scheduling and coordination belong in the orchestrator.
Call blocking vendor SDKs, serial ports or COM/.NET code from worker threads or processes.
Bridge Started / Running / Finished / Cancelled into the orchestrator's state machine so progress and recovery stay observable (C7, C10).
Return structured errors with a stable identifier and context (C3, C16). The same holds for MCP servers: define types, units and output schemas deliberately.
A drop-in simulator with fault injection lets others build and test against your connector before touching hardware (C14).
